subject: Post-call: ACME Health capacity & isolation roadmap
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Joe Smith <joe.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed path: capacity, isolation, SLAs

Joe — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery + the path I propose so we keep momentum. I tried to keep this short and action-oriented.

Pain points you shared:
- Burst traffic (weekly peak windows) causes unpredictable latency and throttling on your current provider.
- Regulatory requirement: HIPAA + regional residency for PHI-heavy workflows.
- Need for predictable monthly spend and clear SLOs for patient-facing endpoints.

Goals we aligned on:
- Baseline reserved capacity that covers steady-state inference (target 99th %ile latency < 200ms for short prompts).
- Burst/overflow policy that preserves availability during spikes without blowing budget.
- Single-tenant isolation for the PHI pipeline and audit logging available for SOC2/HIPAA evidence.

Initial sizing & SLA targets (ballpark):
- Baseline: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (quantized models, KV caching) to meet throughput requirements for daytime traffic.
- Burst: autoscale policy up to +150% capacity using pre-warmed burst slots.
- SLA: 99.9% regional uptime for reserved pool; latency SLOs at 99th percentile as above; audit log retention 12 months (can extend).

Risks & questions to resolve:
- Exact token distribution and long-context usage (affects memory/KV sizing). Can you share 3 representative prompt/response pairs?
- KMS/HSM and SSO requirements — procurement needs to confirm key management approach.
- Procurement window: you mentioned a tight Q4 calendar — who on your side owns PO/contract signoff?

Next steps (owners & timeline):
1) Technical deep-dive (Marissa) — we propose 60m session next week to run through prompt shapes, metrics to capture, and baseline throughput tests. (Owner: Marissa Cole — target: 2026-09-15)
2) Draft SOW + preliminary cost estimate (Marcus) — I attached a short SLA draft + rough capacity spreadsheet. (Owner: Marcus Lin — target: 2026-09-10)
3) Security / compliance kickoff (Jordan) — questionnaire and KMS options. (Owner: Jordan Blake — target: 2026-09-13)

Attachments: 20260908-redwood-sla-draft.pdf (SLA highlights), capacity-rough-estimate.xlsx (ballpark numbers).

If this matches your view, please reply with availability for the technical deep-dive and the PO/contract owner so we can align timelines.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Joe Smith <joe.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap & proposed path: capacity, isolation, SLAs — technical notes

Joe — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: very glad you called out long-context usage. A few concrete items we'll cover in the session: 
- Prompt taxonomy: short routing (<=512 tokens) vs long-analysis (>=2048 tokens). Long-analysis will push KV cache needs and decrease effective batch sizes.
- Recommendation: separate the PHI-sensitive pipeline onto a dedicated model variant (single-tenant pool) with quantization (int8/4) to reduce memory. Use prefix caching for common templates.
- Autoscale & burst: pre-warmed burst slots reduce cold-start latency — suggest 2 pre-warmed nodes that can be fanned out instantly for the first 30s of spikes.
- Ops hooks: tracing + token-level cost reports per API key; set up synthetic traffic checks for SLOs.

Rough capacity note (very approximate) based on your call: baseline 4 x A100-e or equivalent -> expect ~1800 short prompts/min (512-token avg) with KV caching and batching. Long-context analysis will require +50-100% memory headroom. I will bring a short spreadsheet to model expected RPS vs GPU counts in the call.

Attached: capacity-rough-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet with scenarios).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
